title.narrative: Promoting Freedom of Expression and Supporting Safety of Journalists in Yemen

description.narrative: After 8 years of conflict, Yemeni media are highly polarized and Yemeni journalists are facing increased pressure while doing their work including threats, intimidation and surveillance, as well as harassment and attacks. When journalists cannot safely perform their duties, access to an unbiased information and freedom of expression are threatened. Journalists in Yemen suffers from both arbitrary arrests and high level of impunity. Since the beginning of the conflict, 37 journalists have been killed in Yemen without any judicial follow-up. Since 2014, four journalists are imprisoned and were convicted arbitrarily by the court, receiving the death sentence in 2020. UNESCO will continue to raise awareness on the norms and policies related with freedom of expression, press freedom and safety of journalists especially on women journalists' safety amongst duty bearers and right holders in Yemen. UNESCO's support will include capacity building for journalists and media students (continuation of the ongoing training of Universities on the UNESCO Model Course on Safety), as well as raising awareness through the celebration at the national level of the WPFD and IDEI.
